title: Global grid map takes 7.3s on rockerarm: profile the stage and speed up the Newton relaxation
description:
On ixdar-app/test/resources/quadlayout/figure_8/rockerarm_in_tri.off (80818 triangles) QuadLayoutEngine.buildGlobalGridMap reports `[quad-layout] global grid map 7.282s` while every other stage of the pipeline is milliseconds (`patch surfaces 0.007s`). The only other evidence is `[global-grid] relax 1.42e+19→4.63e+04 it=99`. Nothing inside the stage is timed separately, so the first job is to find out where the time goes.

What the stage does, in order (QuadLayoutEngine.buildGlobalGridMap): GridMapAssembly (per-patch rectangle maps, framing into one integer grid, DOF system and sparsity), NewtonSolverNode → GridMapDofSystem.relax → GridMapOptimizer.build (gatherTriangles, buildSparsityPattern, then NewtonRelaxation.run), GridMapIsoSurface.build, then GridMapAssembly.extractQuads which runs GridMapVerification, QuadMeshExtraction and ExtractedPatchGrids and finally converts the quad mesh to an ArrayMesh.

The Newton loop is the prime suspect but not proven. Facts from NewtonRelaxation: the cap is 10000 iterations and a 60s budget, so `it=99` means it stopped on the stall test (STALL_LIMIT=3 consecutive iterations under CONVERGENCE=1e-4 relative improvement) or on a zero accepted step, not on a cap. Each iteration does a full parallel Hessian/gradient assembly (up to MAX_WORKER_THREADS=8 workers over 80k SymmetricDirichletEnergy elements), a numeric refactorization of the ~80k-DOF system on the retained AMD symbolic factor, a solve, and an Armijo line search with up to MAX_BACKTRACKS=5 full energy evaluations, each bounded by the flip-avoiding maximumStep. Starting from an energy of 1.4e19 (symmetric Dirichlet blows up on near-degenerate starting triangles) the flip-avoiding step bound keeps early steps tiny, so many iterations are spent crawling out of the bad region before Newton's quadratic convergence kicks in. ITERATION_LOG_STRIDE=1 also prints a log line every iteration.

Candidate speedups, to be ranked by the profile: (a) a better starting map so the symmetric Dirichlet start is not 1.4e19 (per-patch Tutte maps are flip-free but can be arbitrarily distorted; a few LSCM or ARAP sweeps per patch before assembling could cut the iteration count); (b) a cheaper line search: evaluate the energy on the changed elements only, or reuse the assembled Hessian for a quadratic model on the first backtracks; (c) confirm which DirectSolver backend the grid system actually uses (PARDISO vs the pure-Java Cholesky) and whether the refactorization dominates; (d) check that the assembly workers really run in parallel on the worker pool and are not serialized by the reduction; (e) the three post-relax builds (iso surface, verification, quad extraction) may be non-trivial at 80k triangles and are not timed at all.
definition-of-done: 1. buildGlobalGridMap logs a per-substage time (assembly, relax split into gather/sparsity/Newton, iso surface, verification, extraction) so the breakdown is visible on every run. 2. The Newton relax log line states why it stopped (stall, zero step, cap, budget) and the mean per-iteration time. 3. The profile on rockerarm is written on the ticket with the dominant cost named. 4. At least one of the candidate speedups is implemented and the stage on rockerarm drops to under 2s with the same final energy (4.63e4 ± 1%) and zero flipped triangles. 5. hand (figure_6), botijo and elk (figure_8) report equal or faster times with unchanged energies.
testing-plan: 1. Add the substage timers and run rockerarm; record the breakdown. 2. If the Newton loop dominates, log per-iteration assembly / refactor / solve / line-search times for the first 10 and last 10 iterations, plus the number of backtracks per iteration. 3. Implement the top-ranked fix and re-run. 4. Compare energyAfter, flipped count and worstMove before and after; capture a screenshot of the relaxed grid under tmp/. 5. Run the gridmap and solver tests under ixdar-app/src/test.
todos: DONE : Get the grid-map stage under 2s on rockerarm: the remaining 56 Newton iterations each pay a ~46ms PARDISO numeric refactorization. Two routes, neither attempted here: (1) a fill-reducing ordering better than the AMD port for a 2D mesh Laplacian - nested dissection typically halves nnz(L), and PARDISO can compute its own if IPARM_INDEX_USER_PERMUTATION is turned off, which means reworking DirectSolver.valueSources; (2) a lagged Hessian that reuses the numeric factor across the flip-bounded iterations, where the accepted step is 0.1-0.7 and the Hessian barely moves - safe (the PSD Hessian still gives a descent direction and Armijo still guarantees decrease) but it trades iteration count for factorization count, and the estimate is only 20-30%.

DONE : Optional, small: the starting map's 1.42e19 comes from 7 harmonic-map slivers (worst areaScale 1.4e-05 in patch 180 of rockerarm). Clamping negative cotangent weights in PatchRectangleMap would keep Tutte's flip-free guarantee and likely remove them, saving the ~13 remaining barrier iterations (~23%).

DONE : Buddha (figure_10, 1.55M faces) spends about 75 s in the global grid map stage once PATCH-105 lets it reach that stage (measured by the PATCH-105 agent). Use it as the second benchmark after rockerarm; the ordering and lagged-Hessian routes above matter far more at that size.
changes-made: Profile of buildGlobalGridMap on rockerarm (80818 gathered triangles, 40499 slots / 80998 DOFs, headless quad-layout scene): assembly 0.58-1.13s, relax 10.14s, extract 0.29s, stage 11.55s. Inside relax: gather 0.03s, sparsity 0.12s, iso surface 0.01s, Newton 9.72s. Inside Newton (99 iterations, mean 98.2ms): numeric PARDISO refactorization 63.9ms, solve 18.0ms, parallel assembly 12.8ms, flip-avoiding step bound 1.8ms, line-search energy 0.8ms, backtracks 0. Inside extract: verification 0.02s, iso surface 0.03s, quad mesh 0.21s, patch grids 0.02s. DOMINANT COST: the numeric Cholesky refactorization, 65% of the Newton loop and 55% of the whole stage, multiplied by the iteration count.

Candidate ranking after the profile: (c) the backend is PARDISO (MKL) and the refactorization does dominate, but it is already multi-threaded (MKL_NUM_THREADS=1/4/8 gives 144/52/46ms per refactorization), so there is no threading headroom; (b) the line search was NOT expensive - 0.8ms of 98ms, zero backtracks - it was too TIMID; (d) the assembly reduction is 12% of a 12.8ms assembly, ~1.2ms per iteration; (e) the post-relax builds total 0.29s. Everything reduces to the iteration count.

Root cause of the 99 iterations: iterations 0-53 drop the energy by exactly 43.75% each, with step=1.0 accepted at once while the flip bound allowed 3-30. That factor is Newton on a 1/det^2 barrier: the full Newton step opens a collapsed triangle by 4/3, so the energy falls by (3/4)^2 = 0.5625 per factorization. The cap at step 1 - not the flip bound - was what made the escape cost 54 factorizations.

Fix (NewtonRelaxation.takeStep): after the Armijo test accepts a step, grow it geometrically (EXPANSION=2.0, MAX_EXPANSIONS=12) while the energy still falls, never past MAX_STEP_MARGIN*alphaMax. Untouched wherever alphaMax <= 1.25, so the flip-bounded and final quadratic phases behave exactly as before. rockerarm: 99 -> 56 iterations, stage 11.553s -> 5.422s (2.13x), Newton 9.722s -> 4.328s, energy 4.6332e4 -> 4.6330e4 (0.004% change, inside the 1% bound), flipped 0/80818, worstMove 14.0124 -> 14.0162. elk: 37 -> 35 iterations, stage 2.266s -> 1.600s, energy 4.0274e4 unchanged, flipped 0/32292. Measured back to back on the same machine load; a golden-section refinement of the accepted step was also tried and removed - it changed the iteration count by zero, so the capped step was already at the 1-D minimum.

Instrumentation now permanent: QuadLayoutEngine logs 'global grid map: assembly/relax/extract'; GridMapAssembly.extractQuads logs verification/isoSurface/quadMesh/patchGrids; GridMapDofSystem.relax logs optimize/isoSurface; GridMapOptimizer logs gather/sparsity/newton, the starting-energy concentration, and which triangle blocked the most line searches; NewtonRelaxation logs a '[newton] stop=<reason> iterations=N total=Xs mean=Yms (assemble/refactor/solve/stepLimit/energy) backtracks=B' line, and every iteration line now carries its backtrack count and wall time. Stop reasons are stall / zero-step / iteration-cap / time-budget.

NOT MET: definition-of-done item 4's 2s target. The stage lands at 5.4s on rockerarm, not under 2s. 43 of the remaining 56 iterations are flip-bounded (step = 0.8*alphaMax with alphaMax 0.1-0.8) and the blocking triangle changes almost every iteration (the worst single blocker held back only 2 of 56 searches), so no local fix unblocks them; at an irreducible ~46ms per PARDISO numeric refactorization that is a 2.6s floor for the Newton loop alone. Getting under 2s needs either far fewer factorizations or far fewer iterations - see the new todos.

hand (figure_6) and botijo are unchanged: both still fail upstream of the grid map on the capped-step and grown-step builds alike - hand with an NPE on edgeHit.parametricDelta in the motorcycle stage (PATCH-109), botijo with ArrangementDiagnosticException on arc 4824 in the embedding. Neither reaches buildGlobalGridMap, so there is no grid-map time to compare.

Tests: new ixdar-app/test/unit/mesh/NewtonRelaxationStepGrowthTest.java (mesh-free, analytic 1/x^2 barrier) asserts the grown step reaches the minimum in <=12 iterations where the capped step needs ~32, and that a truncated run reports stop=iteration-cap. Full unit suite green: 224 tests, 0 failures.

Unknowns answered. (1) The 7.3s splits assembly 0.6-1.1s / Newton relax 9.7s / post-relax extraction 0.29s; inside Newton the numeric refactorization is 65%. (2) The time was uniform across iterations, not concentrated: every one of the 99 iterations paid a full assembly + refactorization + solve, and 54 of them bought exactly 43.75% of the energy each because the step was capped at 1 while the flip bound allowed 3-30. (3) The 1.42e19 start is a handful of slivers, not a patch and not a global scale error: 7 of 80818 triangles carry 90% of it, the worst being 4.45e18 in patch 180 at areaScale 1.4e-05, while the middle triangle sits at a healthy areaScale of 0.507.
